answer_1.quote: Assessing the quality of summarizers ... In many text generation scenarios, assessing model quality is arduous ... Standard automatic evaluation methods for summarization rely on the idea that a good summary should have some (semantic) overlap ... We introduce a task-oriented evaluation setup where summaries are meant to allow an agent to perform downstream tasks without reading the longer source text.

answer_2.quote: For all summaries, we evaluate the quality estimation metrics obtained by computing reference-free versions of the ROUGE-L, BERTScore and BARTScore between the source texts and the summaries. We also compare the MI to metrics trained on human judgments and show that it displays consistent correlations.

answer_4.quote: While the SummEval dataset provides only a very limited number of human judgments, it contains enough aligned source, and AI-generated summaries to evaluate the MI metric. ... we compare this ranking with the human evaluation provided by the SummEval benchmark.
answer_4.guideline: Human raters evaluated generated summaries and provided scores that are used as reference judgments for comparison.
